title: 2008 HMMT February Guts Problem 1
statement: Determine all pairs \((a, b)\) of real numbers such that \(10, a, b, a b\) is an arithmetic progression.

solutions.text: \((4,-2),\left(\frac{5}{2},-5\right)\) Since \(10, a, b\) is an arithmetic progression, we have \(a=\frac{1}{2}(10+b)\). Also, we have \(a+a b=2 b\), and so \(a(1+b)=2 b\). Substituting the expression for \(a\) gives \((10+b)(1+b)=4 b\). Solving this quadratic equation gives the solutions \(b=-2\) and \(b=-5\). The corresponding values for \(a\) can be found by \(a=\frac{1}{2}(10+b)\).
